oewn-10145714-n.learner: a person who starts something, causes it, or sets it going
examples: Everyone knew that Tom was the source of the whole plan.

oewn-07273332-n.learner: a book or other published work, or a part of one, that someone refers to
examples: The footnote gives the source of the quotation.

oewn-05843082-n.learner: anything that gives ideas for work that comes later
examples: The old legend was the source for several later plays.

oewn-13580156-n.learner: in technology, a process by which energy or a material comes into a system
examples: The pipe acts as a source of carbon dioxide for the tank.

oewn-04270724-n.learner: a place or building where you can get something
examples: The town library is a good source of free films.

oewn-09430745-n.learner: any person, animal, plant or substance in which a germ that causes disease usually lives and grows in number
examples: Scientists think that bats are the source of the virus.

oewn-06371284-n.learner: letters or signs that are written or printed on a surface to stand for the sounds or words of a language
examples: The writing on the old stone was too worn to read.

oewn-06375185-n.learner: all the works of one author taken together, usually called 'writings'
examples: She has read all the writings of her favourite poet.

oewn-02216885-v.learner: to get something by trading, by giving something up, or by exchanging something for it
examples: She bought her freedom by giving up her share of the farm.

oewn-02652841-v.learner: to be worth something, or to be enough to pay for it
examples: Ten pounds will buy a good pair of boots.

oewn-13985834-n.learner: the lack of life, or the state of being dead
examples: His face was calm and still in death.

oewn-15168437-n.learner: the time when something comes to an end
examples: From its birth to its death, the club met every Friday.
The king ordered that the traitors be put to death.

oewn-14586552-n.learner: the last state that something comes to
examples: Too much rain was the death of our garden.

oewn-00037483-n.learner: something a person has done that is worth noticing
examples: The new bridge was the young engineer's finest effort.

oewn-01623891-v.learner: to put a stop to something
examples: The bad news ended all our hopes.

oewn-13919062-n.learner: a hollow in a surface made by pressing on it
examples: The ring left a small impression in the soft clay.

oewn-00550143-n.learner: a copy of how a person looks or acts that gives a general feel of them rather than exact detail
examples: He did a funny impression of our old teacher.

oewn-06868257-n.learner: a mark or sign made by printing or engraving
examples: The printed impression of the crest was faint on the old page.

oewn-00114352-n.learner: the act of pressing one thing onto or into the surface of another
examples: The impression of the seal into the hot wax took only a second.

oewn-06602491-n.learner: all the copies of a work that were printed at one time
examples: The first impression of the novel sold out in a week.

oewn-03570029-n.learner: in dentistry, a copy of the shape of the teeth and gums made in wax or plaster
examples: The dentist took an impression of her teeth.

oewn-05700875-n.learner: something in your mind that tends to affect what you do
examples: Her own doubts were the main influence on her decision.

oewn-00157901-n.learner: the act of making something happen without any direct or visible effort
examples: The change came about through quiet influence rather than force.

oewn-02534950-v.learner: to fail to do something, or to leave something undone
examples: She neglected to lock the door when she left.

connotation.why: suggests a duty left undone, against plain 'not do' or 'forget'

oewn-08649106-n.learner: a land or area that is controlled by a ruling country
examples: The island was once a possession of a distant empire.

oewn-04869236-n.learner: the quality of firmly keeping control of how you behave
examples: She never lost possession of herself, even when he insulted her.

oewn-00811363-n.learner: in sport, the act of having control of the ball or puck
examples: Our team kept possession of the ball for most of the game.

oewn-09205421-n.learner: a mania about just one thing or idea
examples: Collecting old clocks had become a possession with him.

connotation.why: frames a single interest as a mania, against plain 'interest' or 'passion'
